interactions.title: Pip’s stories and the jungle’s silence
lines: DM: ((Approach to the tree))Pip, the fruit bat who guided you towards where she found the jade was full of stories as she flew, telling you about well, what she learned as a child only a few years ago, as she learned to talk as she learned to fly, not really knowing anything about the history of the jungle, and not really thinking it strange that she could speak elvish. But you heard tales from her of the mango trees that sing ballads when their fruit is ripe, calling her and her people and her companions to come feast; of the trickster monkeys who live on the mangroves on the coast, protected by Slither, an ancient boa constrictor, who run around the jungle howling news and gossip to everybody, but have been quiet of late; the orchids that bloom and whisper love poems to hummingbirds; the groves of banyan trees that speak in many voices, turning the stories of the jungle into dramatic plays. The Fire Clan, led by the Tiger Blaze, who live along the Big River to the west, keeping a watchful eye.

DM: So as Pip is telling these stories, and you're flying through the jungle, what you're passing through is nothing like the story she tells. The trees are quiet. You don't hear any mango trees singing ballads, or booming gossip of howler monkeys, or whispered poems of humming—of orchids, or even the buzz of insects, seems dulled or muted.

DM: Now, as Pip returns to her family and friends in the cave, after showing you where she found the jade, the silence is even more oppressive and quiet without her chattering high pitched tales to keep you company.
